stories.notes: Empty acceptance criteria on a complex cross-platform (GO, UP, MX) live preview feature. Openspec needed first to elaborate requirements — define what 'live preview' means across all three contexts, state synchronization model, and rendering approach. Speckit then hardens for testability, iframe sandboxing/XSS security, real-time sync edge cases, and cross-platform consistency checks. No existing spec or hand-curation detected, so full spec pipeline is warranted.

agentContributions.notes: Live Preview is a new capability — Contentstack's live-preview integration allows CMS editors to see real-time content changes in a preview iframe without manual refresh. The central attachment point is useContent (236+ callers), which is where content fetching happens and where a live-preview listener/re-fetch mechanism must plug in. No existing live-preview code was found in the indexed symbols. VCs are derived solely from the description since ACs are empty, and are scoped to our side of the Contentstack boundary.

Openspec provided empty acceptanceCriteria, so all criteria are new. I could not read the four source files (useContent.ts, contentstack.ts, contentCard.ts, ContentstackLink.tsx), so AC-8 about multi-site uniformity and AC-2 about non-preview parity may need refinement once the actual useContent hook signature and Contentstack service layer are known. AC-6 (origin validation) assumes Contentstack's live-preview protocol uses postMessage; if it uses a different mechanism (e.g., WebSocket or polling), the security criterion should be adjusted to validate that mechanism instead. AC-5 (debounce) threshold of 500ms is a reasonable starting point but should be validated with the team. AC-9 (accessibility) and AC-10 (visual indicator) address WCAG perceptibility requirements for dynamic content changes. AC-11 addresses bundle-size concern since live-preview is a development/CMS-only feature.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: All four manifest paths (src/hooks/useContent.ts, src/services/contentstack.ts, src/interface/content/contentCard.ts, src/components/contentstack/ContentstackLink/ContentstackLink.tsx) are confirmed to EXIST — no missing_manifest_path flag. Both agents added meaningful, non-overlapping value: openspec identified the central integration point (useContent hook, 236+ callers), defined the live-preview scope, and bounded it to our side of the Contentstack boundary; speckit hardened for security (origin validation, iframe sandboxing/XSS), edge cases (debounce, accessibility, bundle-size isolation), and perceptibility (WCAG). However, speckit explicitly states it could not read the four source files, meaning AC-2 (non-preview parity) and AC-8 (multi-site uniformity) are based on assumptions about the codebase rather than verified code. AC-6 assumes postMessage as the live-preview transport; if Contentstack uses a different mechanism (WebSocket/polling), the security criterion may be inapplicable. AC-5's 500ms debounce threshold is unvalidated. These are genuine gaps that should be resolved by a human who can inspect the actual useContent hook signature and Contentstack service layer before implementation begins.
